checks.claim: NASA says it will put a nuclear reactor on the Moon by the first quarter of fiscal year 2030, and has asked industry for a design of at least 100 kilowatts electric with a closed Brayton power cycle.
checks.evidence: NASA's January 2026 release on the DOE partnership (fetched) says the agencies will pursue 'including the development of a lunar surface reactor by 2030' and 'to develop, fuel, authorize, and ready a lunar surface reactor for launch'. It gives no fiscal-year or first-quarter date and no power level. The fiscal 2030 date and the 100 kWe figure come from NASA's August 2025 request for information, which I did not fetch. The release does not say the reactor will be placed on the Moon.

sources.label: NASA — NASA, Department of Energy to Develop Lunar Surface Reactor by 2030 (January 2026)
sources.quote: to develop, fuel, authorize, and ready a lunar surface reactor for launch

checks.review: Overruled (main session): the agent read only the January 2026 release. The row's first source, NASA Glenn's RFI page (cached), says NASA 'declared its intent to put a nuclear reactor on the Moon by the first quarter of fiscal year 2030' and gives the 100 kWe floor.

applications.name: Alva (Jyväskylä city-owned utility) nuclear district heating study with Steady Energy
applications.power_class: 50 MWt per LDR-50 reactor (design); unit count for Jyväskylä not published
applications.timeline: letter of intent announced 2026-05-19; one-year preliminary study to follow
applications.what_it_says: Steady Energy and Alva, Jyväskylä's city-owned utility, signed a letter of intent in May 2026 to look at small reactors as a district heat source for the city. The LDR-50 is a 50 MW thermal design running at about 150 °C, and the announcement does not say how many units Jyväskylä could take. The year-long study covers regulation, sites, technology and costs.
applications.microreactor_read: A 50 MWt-class heat plant is far larger than the 1-20 MW block this tab tracks, and this is a letter of intent for a city heat network. The next gates are the one-year study and Finnish licensing, neither of which has a date.

applications.name: Helen (Helsinki district heat utility) letter of intent with Steady Energy
applications.power_class: up to 10 units at 50 MWt each (LDR-50)
applications.timeline: letter of intent reported 3 October 2023; no construction date given
applications.what_it_says: Helen, a Finnish energy firm, signed a letter of intent with Steady Energy to enable investment in a small-scale nuclear plant for district heating. The letter would let Helen procure up to ten LDR-50 reactor units, each with a 50 MW output.
applications.microreactor_read: Ten 50 MWt units is a city-scale heat network, far above the 1-20 MW block this tab tracks. The source gives no construction date, so this is a 2023 intent that has not been tied to an order.
